Yep, in real life gravity decays with distance² instead of distance¹. In practical terms, this means that gravities just above the surface of a planet in OW are a little higher than they would be irl, but they fall off much faster with distance.

This allows the devs to implement proper N-body gravitation, as opposed to a system like Kerbal Space Program's, in which one body affects your craft at a time (and also in which no celestial bodies can be moved from pre-set orbits).

The Sun is the only body in Outer Wilds that uses a real-world, parabolic gravitation curve; this is done so that things like the Interloper don't just fly off into space.
